name: Reza Shah
role: Shah of Iran (1925–1941); earlier army commander and prime minister
summary: Reza Shah pursued centralized royal authority, military consolidation and state-led modernization. He promoted Persian national culture and curtailed clerical authority, while suppressing political opposition and imposing social reforms through coercion.

notes:
No inferred answers. The seven-chapter Persian travelogue was downloaded and searched across the statement themes; its dictated first-person text is distinguished from publisher introductions. Chapters 3 and 5 were also read for context. Formal assent alone is not used as evidence. Later secondhand accounts are medium at most. The later White Revolution, women’s suffrage, forest nationalization and post-1956 conservation measures belong to his son’s period and are not assigned to him. Support for a women’s congress does not establish every demand adopted there. The coronation speech preserves religion as a source of unity, while the diary rejects its fusion with politics; this does not establish atheism or a comprehensive position on every religious liberty. Modern technology advocacy does not establish that technology solves most human problems. No inclusion padding; remaining statements reviewed against the full list.

Merged with an independent claude-sonnet-5-5 audit: 9 answers taken from it, 19 agreed, 0 conflicts settled by the integrator.

claude-sonnet-5-5 notes: Independent second audit; reached by sources other than the first audit's Persian travelogue and Iranica set. Searched by theme: government (elections, parliament, press, cabinet, army), world (oil, capitulations, neutrality), society (clergy, conscription). Primary sources are scarce in English: no speech collection or memoir could be opened, so most answers rest on scholarly reports of his record (medium at most). Many answers describe acts of his government that scholars tie to him (oil cancellation, the 1924 election rigging, conscription decree); the banking and capital-control answers rest on measures by his team and are weaker. Not found or not opened: Iranica articles (blocked by Cloudflare), Chehabi on dress (paywalled), so unveiling, language, education, minorities and women's issues are left null.
